data.title: U.S. Dollar Ticks Higher Amid Inflation Data Release, Expectations Of Reopening Of Strait Of Hormuz
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - The U.S. Dollar value inched higher as investors weighed today's inflation data that pushed the odds for a rate hike in the U.S. higher against reports of an upcoming meeting between the Gulf Cooperation Council nations and Iran to hasten the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

Today, the U.S. Dollar Index DXY, which measures the Greenback against a basket of other major currencies, was last seen trading at 99.13, down by 0.05 (or 0.05%).

While against the Euro, the USD was trading at 1.159, up by 0.12%, against the GBP, the USD was trading at 1.352, down by 0.12%.

Against the USD, the Japanese Yen was trading at 153.509, up by 0.59%, the Swiss Franc was trading at 0.816, down by 0.46%; and the Canadian Dollar was trading at 1.387, down by 0.29%.

Against one unit of Australian Dollar, the USD was trading at 0.716, down by 0.18%.

Today, the data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics revealed that, on a month-on-month basis, the Consumer Price Index increased 0.40% in August. On a year-on-year basis, the CPI steadied at 3.40% in August, unchanged from July. Both these prints came in line with market expectations.

Further, on a month-on-month basis, the core Consumer Price Index in the U.S. (which excludes food and energy) increased by 0.30% in August. On a year-on-year basis, the core CPI eased to 2.40% in August.

The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer sentiment index fell to 47.80 in September, weaker than market expectations.

Yesterday's data revealed that on a month-on-month basis, the Producer Price Index increased 0.40% in August and on a year-on-year basis, it increased 5.40%.

U.S. Labor Department data revealed that on a month-on-month basis, the core Producer Price Index (which excludes food and energy sectors), increased 0.20% from the previous month in August. For the same month, on a year-on-year basis, the core PPI inched up to 4.60%.

Currently, investors are betting on a 86.50% chance of a 25-basis-point interest rate-hike at the upcoming meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve on September 15-16 while the odds on rates being held at the current level stand at 13.50%, according to the CME Group's FedWatch Tool.

A report by Financial Times today indicated that the foreign ministers of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) are set to meet their Iranian counterpart in the coming week.

The meeting is intended to secure a deal with Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz for commercial shipping as well as to de-escalate the Middle East crisis.

Following the news, crude oil prices tumbled by more than 2.00%.

The member countries of the GCC in the Arabian Peninsula, namely Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, and Bahrain suffered from the retaliatory attacks by Iran during the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict.

All these nations produce crude oil but have paused or minimized production due to the disability in exporting the output after Iran shut the Strait of Hormuz.

According to the FT report, this initiative is undertaken by Oman with the meeting slated to be held in the coastal city of Salalah on Monday.

The Strait of Hormuz remains shut since the end of February when the U.S.-Iran conflict began which is showing no sign of de-escalation.

U.S. and Iran have stepped up their attacks on each other's targets in the recent weeks.

data.title: Marvell is sitting on an incredibly 'sticky' business that could help it unlock a $30 billion opportunity
data.description:
By Britney Nguyen

Marvell is best known for making custom chips - but an analyst notes there's arguably more potential in supporting components and optical networking

Marvell's stock is up 178% so far this year.

Marvell Technology's custom chips and connectivity offerings have made it a major beneficiary of the data-center build-out - so much so that one analyst is touting the company as a paragon of "accelerating multiengine growth."

Marvell's (MRVL) end-to-end portfolio for data-center connectivity "layers on more customers and products each year," Bank of America analyst Vivek Arya said, and he sees that driving rapid growth in the company's revenue and earnings per share.

Arya said Marvell sees its "XPU attach" business as "much stickier" than its XPU business, meaning customers are returning to and engaging with those offerings more. Marvell refers to its custom chips as XPUs, and to the components that support them in data centers - such as networking and storage controllers - as XPU attach.

If each custom chip has one or more sockets - or places on the processor where it connects to other components - and each component can sell for an average price of between $500 to $1,500, Arya said that Marvell could see $30 billion in revenue from XPU attach by the end of the decade. By that point, he expects the total addressable market for supporting chip components to reach between $60 billion and $65 billion - or even more.

The analyst noted that Marvell expects its lead custom-chip customer, Amazon Web Services (AMZN), to continue growing each year. The chip maker also plans to start ramping custom products with Microsoft (MSFT) next year, which he said will help Marvell gain share in the market for custom chips. Arya sees the total addressable market for custom computing offerings, including both chips and the components that support them, reaching about $300 billion by the end of the decade.

Meanwhile, he said, Marvell stands to win the market for scale-up optical networking "regardless of how customers choose to build," given its portfolio of co-packaged optics, near-packaged optics and near-packaged optical components. Scale-up networking connects several processors together to work as a singular, more powerful chip.

Arya added that Marvell doesn't see a threat to its optics business from Amazon's recent announcement to work with Qualcomm (QCOM) on optical-connectivity components.

Marvell's stock was down fractionally Friday, but is still up nearly 178% so far this year.

-Britney Nguyen

data.title: Michael Burry Sells FLUT To Pile Into LULU Under $100 — Plus A New Bet On ZTS
data.description:
Key points:
  • Burry exited his Flutter position in full, citing relative valuation.
  • He believes LULU’s management problems could make the company an acquisition target.
  • He increased his Zoetis position "in the $72s," calling the stock “very cheap.”

“The Big Short” investor Michael Burry has sold his Flutter Entertainment Plc (FLUT) position in full and moved the majority of the proceeds into Lululemon Athletica Inc. (LULU), while also increasing his stake in Zoetis Inc. (ZTS).

Burry said Flutter was no longer as attractive relative to the valuations of other stocks, called Lululemon’s valuation increasingly “compressed,” and described Zoetis as “very cheap.”

At the time of writing on Friday, FLUT was trading 1.5% lower in after-hours trading after ending the regular session nearly 2% higher. LULU was up 0.09%, while ZTS was trading 0.3% higher.

Burry Exits FLUT, Moves Into LULU

Burry said he sold Flutter in its entirety because the stock was “not as attractive at this price relative to the valuations to which some other stocks have fallen.”

He said he then “piled the majority” of the proceeds into Lululemon under $100.

“I imagine LULU, as profitable as it is, and as compressed as its valuation has become, may not be public for very much longer,” Burry wrote in a post on Substack.

Burry stressed that he has “no information” that Lululemon could be taken private. However, he added that the company’s problems have “largely been due to bad management” and that he believes there are others that could “easily buy it and run it much better.”

“Hence, my urgency,” Burry added.

Burry Adds To ZTS, But Has A Warning

Burry also said he bought more Zoetis (ZTS) in the $72s, which he believes is “very cheap for this company.”

He said Zoetis is trying to “put in a base here on high volume,” but warned that the stock “may bleed lower.”

FLUT, LULU, ZTS Stocks: Stocktwits Retail Sentiment

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment for LULU shifted to ‘neutral’ from ‘extremely bullish’ over the past 24 hours. Sentiment for FLUT remained ‘bearish,’ while ZTS stayed ‘extremely bearish,’ with neither changing over the same period.

Message volume for LULU was ‘normal,’ while it was ‘low’ for both FLUT and ZTS.

Year-to-date, FLUT has declined nearly 54%, LULU has lost more than 52%, and ZTS is down more than 42%.

data.title: Alibaba Gains as Anthropic Alleges 151 Million Illicit Exchanges
data.description:
Alibaba Group Holding , China's e-commerce and cloud-computing giant, rose approximately 0.7% to $109.42 Friday despite allegations that operators associated with the company improperly extracted Claude's reasoning capabilities. Reuters said Alibaba did not immediately respond to its request for comment. The market's reaction was clear: investors noticed the accusation, but they did not rush for the exit.

Anthropic's company-authored investigation linked more than 151 million exchanges between May and July to what it described as an unauthorized distillation campaign designed to improve Qwen models. Activity reportedly approached three million exchanges per day at its peak and ran through thousands of fraudulent accounts. These are Anthropic's claims, not findings established by a court or regulatora crucial distinction while Alibaba remains publicly silent.

Alibaba's latest results showed AI Cloud and Compute Services revenue climbing 45% to 48.44 billion yuan, roughly 18% of total revenue. The image places Alibaba's $109.42 share price 8.68% below its $119.82 GF Value, suggesting modest upside to that estimate. But the bigger investor question is not mathematical: Alibaba must show that the technology powering its fast-growing AI business was built on a credible and defensible foundation.

data.title: BMO Drops StakeTake On Lululemon Stock
data.description:
Lululemon Athletica faces another sharp warning from Wall Street as BMO Capital Markets initiated coverage with an Underperform rating and a $70 price target, implying roughly 28% downside from Thursday's close. Analyst Kelly Crago argues the athletic-wear retailer is losing relevance with consumers just as competition intensifies and management attempts a difficult turnaround.

Lululemon is a premium athletic-apparel retailer best known for leggings, yoga wear and other performance clothing. The company sells primarily through its own stores and digital channels, with growth historically driven by premium pricing, product innovation and strong customer loyalty.

Crago said that irrelevance with the consumer is showing up in the numbers. She pointed to market-share losses across the Americas and China as brands such as Alo and Vuori gain ground. The product engine that has fueled this company for years is very stale because it's a much tougher category where athleisure is out of favor, Crago added.

The bearish call comes after Lululemon shares plunged 17.4% in a single session to $100.61. The stock has now lost more than 80% from its December 2023 record high of $511.29. Falling store traffic and weaker demand for its core $110 leggings have already forced management to cut its full-year sales outlook three times, with the latest forecast at $10.35 billion versus an original $11.35 billion target.

Investors Takeaway

The biggest test now falls on new CEO Heidi O'Neill, a former Nike executive who began her tenure this week. Second-quarter store sales fell 9%, while BMO expects fiscal-2027 earnings per share of just $6.35, below Wall Street consensus.

Investors should watch comparable-store sales, traffic trends, inventory clearance and whether fresh products can reverse market-share losses. Continued discounting would suggest brand power is weakening further, while stabilization in traffic and stronger product launches could undermine BMO's bearish case.

data.title: BMO Tweaks Oracle Stock Price Target After AI Risk
data.description:
Oracle received a lower price target from BMO Capital despite another explosive quarter for its cloud infrastructure business, highlighting a growing investor tension around the AI trade: revenue and backlog are surging, but the economics of delivering that growth remain under scrutiny. BMO analyst Keith Bachman cut his Oracle target to $195 from $220 while maintaining an Outperform rating.

BMO pointed to several positives following Oracle's fiscal first-quarter results, including operating cash flow, operating margins and a reasonable sequential increase in remaining performance obligations. But the bank flagged the sequential decline in gross margins as a potential investor concern and said SaaS growth was somewhat disappointing.

Oracle's underlying growth remains formidable. Fiscal first-quarter revenue jumped 30% year over year to $19.3 billion, while total cloud revenue surged 62% to $11.6 billion. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure revenue soared 121% to $7.4 billion, reflecting enormous demand for AI training and inference capacity.

The weaker point was cloud applications. SaaS revenue increased just 10% to $4.2 billion, creating a sharp contrast with Oracle's infrastructure acceleration.

Oracle's backlog nevertheless provides substantial revenue visibility. Remaining performance obligations reached $664 billion after the company booked more than $30 billion of additional AI cloud contracts during the quarter. Operating cash flow hit a record $23 billion, though aggressive infrastructure investment pushed free cash flow to negative $5 billion.

Investors Takeaway

The central issue is whether Oracle can convert its extraordinary AI backlog into revenue without allowing gross margins and cash generation to deteriorate materially.

Investors should closely watch gross-margin trends, SaaS growth and the pace at which the $664 billion RPO balance converts into sales. Oracle expects second-quarter revenue to grow 30% to 34%, with cloud revenue rising 65% to 71% in reported currency.

Continued triple-digit infrastructure growth alongside stabilizing margins would strengthen BMO's Outperform thesis. But if AI capacity expansion keeps pressuring profitability while slower SaaS growth persists, investors may increasingly question how much of Oracle's massive backlog will ultimately translate into attractive returns.

data.title: UBS Reworks Adobe Price Target For Rest Of The Year
data.description:
Adobe received a higher price target from UBS after its latest earnings report, but the bank stopped short of turning bullish, arguing that steady growth and resilient software demand are still not enough to justify a bigger valuation re-rating. UBS lifted its target to $255 from $225 while maintaining a Neutral rating, leaving only modest upside from Adobe's recent trading level near $248.

Adobe reported fiscal third-quarter revenue growth of roughly 12% to 13%, with quarterly sales reaching $6.76 billion and beating consensus estimates by about $60 million. The company also reaffirmed its fiscal-2026 annual recurring revenue growth guidance of 10% and raised its full-year targets, supported by free cash flow of $2.44 billion.

UBS nevertheless highlighted several weaker areas beneath the headline numbers. Margins, core Creative growth and committed remaining performance obligations all came in somewhat soft, while cRPO growth slowed to 9%. Those results reinforced UBS's view that Adobe and the broader software applications layer remain resilient through the AI transition, but have not yet produced enough upside to warrant a more aggressive stance.

UBS analyst Karl Keirstead wrote that "in our view there was not enough/any real upside to drive a further re-rating and we remain Neutral-rated."

The divided analyst reaction underscores Adobe's current investor debate. Wells Fargo raised its target to $270 on expectations for improving net new ARR, while JPMorgan cut its target to $315 amid monetization concerns. Baird also raised its target but kept a Neutral rating.

Investors Takeaway

The key issue is whether Adobe can turn resilient top-line growth into accelerating ARR and stronger committed backlog growth.

Investors should focus on cRPO trends, core Creative growth, margins and net new ARR. Improvement across those metrics could support a valuation re-rating and push the stock beyond UBS's $255 target.

If growth remains steady but uninspiring, however, Adobe may continue to trade as a durable software franchise without the upside investors once assigned to faster growth and AI-driven monetization.

data.title: Colgate Weighs $1 Billion Brand Sale in Portfolio Revamp
data.description:
Colgate-Palmolive is exploring the sale of several well-known personal-care brands in a potential transaction worth more than $1 billion, signaling a sharper effort to streamline its portfolio as North American growth remains under pressure. For investors, divesting slower-growth mass-market brands could free capital for Colgate's stronger businesses while sharpening management's focus on improving profitability and organic growth.

Colgate-Palmolive is one of the world's largest consumer-products companies, best known for Colgate toothpaste and other oral-care products. It also sells personal-care, home-care and pet-nutrition products, with oral care accounting for nearly half of company sales.

The company is working with Goldman Sachs on a possible divestiture of brands including Softsoap, Irish Spring and Speed Stick, according to Reuters. The assets under review represent only part of Colgate's personal-care business and could collectively fetch more than $1 billion.

The move comes amid a broader consumer-goods portfolio reset. Companies including Unilever and Nestle have been selling noncore businesses as tariffs, higher input costs and financially stretched consumers pressure earnings. Asset sales can allow companies to concentrate resources behind brands with stronger pricing power and growth prospects.

Colgate's own numbers underline the strategic challenge. The company has a market value of roughly $70 billion, and its shares are up about 11% this year. Most recently, net sales increased 4.9%, but North American organic sales fell 3%. CEO Noel Wallace said improving the business would require a "long-term turnaround."

Investors Takeaway

The biggest near-term catalyst is whether Colgate reaches a deal and what valuation the brands ultimately command.

Investors should also watch North American organic sales, operating margins and how proceeds are redeployed. Personal care represented 17% of 2025 sales, or roughly $3.5 billion, so Colgate is not abandoning the category entirely.

A strong sale price combined with improving North American performance could strengthen the case that portfolio simplification is creating value. Weak buyer interest or continued organic-sales pressure would make the turnaround harder to justify.

data.title: JPMorgan Tweaks Hims & Hers Stock Outlook on Key Risk
data.description:
Hims & Hers Health faces a more complicated growth path as regulatory pressure reshapes its weight-loss business, prompting JPMorgan to resume coverage at Neutral with a $32 price target. The target implies roughly 17% upside from the Sept. 10 close, but the bank wants clearer evidence that Hims can successfully transition from compounded GLP-1 drugs toward branded treatments without sacrificing margins.

Hims & Hers operates a direct-to-consumer telehealth platform offering treatments across weight loss, sexual health, dermatology, mental health and other categories. The company generates revenue primarily through subscriptions and prescription medications delivered through its digital platform.

JPMorgan analyst Brian Smilek had previously rated the shares Overweight before coverage was suspended in June. While he remains constructive on Hims' vertical integration and expansion into new specialties and international markets, he said, "we look for execution across the strategic transition toward branded GLP-1s, durability of growth across newer specialties, deeper international penetration, and durable margin expansion."

The biggest near-term challenge is weight-loss economics.

Greater FDA scrutiny has constrained Hims' compounded GLP-1 business, forcing the company to lean more heavily on branded medications. Its partnership with Novo Nordisk , which gives customers access to Wegovy and Ozempic, "should more than offset compounded GLP-1 headwinds," Smilek said.

Hims also offers Eli Lilly treatments including Zepbound and Foundayo.

The tradeoff is profitability. JPMorgan warned that "near-term adjusted EBITDA margins face headwinds from the mix shift toward branded GLP-1s," because branded medicines generally offer less attractive economics than compounded products.

Investors Takeaway

The central question is whether Hims can replace lost compounded-GLP-1 economics with enough branded-drug volume and growth elsewhere to preserve its earnings trajectory.

Investors should monitor branded GLP-1 adoption, adjusted EBITDA margins and growth across newer specialties and international markets. Success in those areas would strengthen the case that Hims is becoming a broader healthcare platform rather than relying heavily on compounded weight-loss drugs.

JPMorgan also sees peptides as another potential growth opportunity. But until Hims proves the transition can support both revenue growth and durable margin expansion, the $32 target suggests upside may remain constrained by execution risk.

data.title: Tesla Gains as Semi Opens a $17 Billion Software Door
data.description:
Diesel prices nearing $6 a gallon sharpened the financial case for Teslas electric truck Friday. Tesla , the electric-vehicle and artificial-intelligence company, climbed approximately 0.7% to $365.865 as Morgan Stanley argued that investors may be overlooking the Semis potential contribution to earnings.

The firm estimates that a fully autonomous Semi could command a Full Self-Driving subscription of $12,000 to $18,000 per monthfar above the roughly $100 charged for consumer vehicles. Its 2040 scenario includes 82,000 Semis generating $17 billion in subscription revenue and $7.5 billion in earnings before interest and taxes. Tesla began volume production in May and is targeting annual capacity of 50,000 trucks.

Those projections point to a striking EBIT margin of roughly 44%, making autonomous software the real prizenot truck sales alone. The picture shows Tesla trading 9.62% above its GF Value of $333.77, suggesting investors already pay a premium for that future potential. Expensive diesel strengthens the pitch today, but Tesla must still deliver commercial heavy-truck autonomy to turn Morgan Stanleys $17 billion vision into an actual business.

data.title: Raymond James Has Strong Message For Rocket Lab Investors
data.description:
Rocket Lab USA shares gained more than 2% in premarket trading after Raymond James initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and an $80 price target, implying roughly 29% upside. Analyst Brian Gesuale sees Rocket Lab evolving beyond its small-launch roots into a vertically integrated space company, with Neutron, spacecraft systems and improving cash flow potentially driving its next stage of growth.

Rocket Lab provides launch services through its Electron rocket while also selling spacecraft, satellite components, payload systems and optical communications technology. That broader model gives the company several potential revenue streams beyond simply sending satellites into orbit.

The bullish call comes as Rocket Lab continues building launch momentum. The company completed its 16th Electron mission of 2026 on Sept. 11, deploying an Earth-observation satellite into low Earth orbit for a confidential customer. The flight marked Rocket Lab's 95th launch overall, with another commercial Electron mission planned before the end of September.

Gesuale sees that launch record as only part of the story. He views Rocket Lab as an emerging vertically integrated space platform spanning launch, spacecraft, components, payloads and optical communications. Neutron, its planned medium-lift rocket, is expected to expand those capabilities in 2027.

RKLB has assembled launch, spacecraft, components, payloads, and optical communications, Gesuale said.

The analyst also expects Rocket Lab's financial profile to improve as investment requirements decline. He projects positive EBITDA and free cash flow around 2027 to 2028.

Investors Takeaway

Neutron is the most important catalyst. Successful development and commercial deployment could move Rocket Lab into the larger medium-lift launch market and materially expand its addressable opportunity.

Investors should also monitor Electron launch cadence, progress toward positive free cash flow and integration of acquired businesses. Rocket Lab's $155.3 million Mynaric acquisition expands its laser-communications capabilities, but Gesuale flagged integration as a risk.

If Neutron stays on schedule while launch activity and space-systems revenue grow, Raymond James' bullish thesis could strengthen. Delays, acquisition problems or continued heavy cash consumption would make that $80 target harder to reach.

data.title: Amazon Gains as S&P Flags Its $100 Billion Debt Spree
data.description:
Amazon , the e-commerce and cloud-computing giant, rose about 1.5% to $255.71 Friday as Wall Street weighed S&P's warning over hyperscaler credit risk. Axios reported that Amazon has tapped bond investors for roughly $100 billion in 2026, supplying fresh fuel for its massive AI infrastructure buildout.

Amazon's second-quarter results show the financial engine behind that borrowing power. AWS revenue jumped 37% to $42.2 billion, while operating income hit $16.6 billion, producing a formidable 39.3% margin. Trailing operating cash flow reached $161.4 billion, but free cash flow swung to negative $7.6 billion as property investment surged. The chart adds a valuation warning: Amazon trades 3.19% above its $247.80 GF Value, leaving little room for execution mistakes.

The $100 billion raised through bonds represents roughly 45% of Amazon's estimated $220 billion annual capital-spending plan. Yet S&P's concern stretches beyond Amazon's own balance sheet. Hyperscalers are also helping bankroll smaller AI companies, tying elite credit profiles to far weaker counterparties. Amazon has the cash machine to keep spending now. The real test is whether AI revenue scales before depreciation, interest expenses and partner commitments all start biting at once.

data.title: Restaurant Brands International Renews Normal Course Issuer Bid
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis

Restaurant Brands International's notice that it will renew its normal course issuer bid for common shares of its stock was accepted by the Toronto Stock Exchange.

The normal course issuer bid is being conducted as part of the company's share repurchase plan for up to $1 billion of its common stock through Sept. 30 of next year, the company said Friday.

Restaurant Brands has a market cap of $34.77 billion, 348.76 million shares outstanding, and a public float of 341.4 million shares.

The company's brands include Popeyes, Tim Hortons, and Burger King.

Shares ended the day's market trading session on the New York Stock Exchange up less than 1% to close at $76.96, and are now up 13% this year. On the Toronto Stock Exchange, shares rose less than 1% on the day and closed at C$106.75.

data.title: Court Strikes Down Order to Keep a Coal-Fired Plant Running — WSJ
data.description:
By Jennifer Hiller

A federal appeals court on Friday struck down a Trump administration order to keep a coal-fired power plant in Michigan running past its planned retirement.

For more than a year, emergency orders from the Department of Energy have kept the J.H. Campbell plant open.

Operating costs are passed to customers. Consumers Energy, which operates the plant, said in a regulatory filing that after revenues from electricity sales, it had cost $259 million to comply with the orders through June.

The company said Friday it is reviewing the ruling and continuing to comply with the latest 90-day order that keeps the plant running.

"Ultimately, we will follow the law and work to ensure that everyone who benefits from power from the Campbell plant across the Midwest pays their fair share," the company said.

ClearView Energy Partners said that it's possible that the D.C. Circuit could vacate similar orders for five other power plants that are the subject of similar emergency orders and litigation.

"The Energy Department's emergency orders, including at Campbell, prevented blackouts and likely saved hundreds of lives during peak capacity events this past year," said Ben Dietderich, DOE spokesperson.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

data.title: Ebola infections top 7,000 in Congo as virus spreads to new province
data.description:
The number of confirmed Ebola cases in Democratic Republic of Congo has passed 7,000, with the virus spreading to a new province, government data showed on Friday.

The outbreak, caused by the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, became the largest and deadliest in Congo's history after surpassing the 2018-2020 epidemic.

It is now second only to the 2014-2016 West African outbreak, which infected over 28,600 people and killed more than 11,000 across Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone.

Government figures showed late on Friday that the death toll had risen to 3,398, while confirmed cases reached 7,022 across seven provinces.

Officials told Reuters earlier on Friday an Ebola case had been detected in South Ubangi province, located in the northwest of the country, far from the epicentre of the outbreak.

Shortages of trained staff, operational partners and funding are causing a bottleneck in efforts ‌to expand the Ebola response, according to the World Health Organization.

data.title: GMR Solutions Inc. Secures Commitments for Term Loan Repricing; Plans $200 Million Debt Paydown
data.description:
GMR Solutions Inc. (“GMR”) (NYSE: GMRS), the nation’s largest provider of emergency medical services, announced that Global Medical Response, Inc., the borrower under its first lien term loan, has obtained binding commitments to complete a repricing of its existing $2.9 billion Term Loan B facility due October 2032. In connection with the transaction, GMR expects to use approximately $200 million of cash on hand to repay outstanding term loan borrowings, reducing the outstanding principal amount of the facility to approximately $2.7 billion upon closing.

The repricing will reduce the applicable interest rate from SOFR +325 basis points to SOFR +275 basis points, reducing the applicable interest rate by 50 basis points.

“This transaction reflects the commitments we made to utilize cash generated by the business to reduce total leverage,” said Brian Tierney, chief financial officer of GMR. “The combination of the repricing and $200 million debt repayment is expected to generate approximately $28 million of annual interest savings, supporting our commitment to reducing leverage while strengthening financial flexibility.”

The transaction is expected to close on or about Sept. 17, 2026, subject to customary closing conditions.

About Global Medical Response

GMR is the nation’s largest provider of emergency medical services (EMS), delivering EMS and other essential out-of-hospital care in rural and urban communities that represent approximately 60% of the U.S. population. As the only national, fully integrated, air and ground EMS provider, GMR operates in approximately 1,400 counties across the country. A recognized innovator, GMR develops new solutions to meet evolving industry needs and expand access to high-quality care. With roughly 34,000 team members, GMR supports nearly 5.5 million patient encounters annually and performs a critical care intervention every 88 seconds. Its family of solutions includes ambulance EMS provider American Medical Response, as well as multiple air EMS organizations including Air Evac Lifeteam, REACH Air Medical Services, Guardian Flight, Med-Trans Corporation, and AirMed International.
